definitions.explanation: A person who lives in a particular place. A formal term used in legal, administrative, and official contexts, as opposed to the more everyday word {住民|じゅうみん}.

examples.japanese: このマンションの{居住者|きょじゅうしゃ}は{約|やく}200{人|にん}だ。
examples.english: This apartment building has about 200 residents.

examples.japanese: {居住者|きょじゅうしゃ}{以外|いがい}の{立|た}ち{入|い}りは{禁止|きんし}されている。
{海外|かいがい}{居住者|きょじゅうしゃ}は{日本|にほん}の{税金|ぜいきん}について{特別|とくべつ}なルールが{適用|てきよう}される{場合|ばあい}がある。
examples.english: Special tax rules may apply to overseas residents in Japan.

notes:
USAGE:
A formal word most commonly seen in legal documents, building rules, government forms, and official notices. In everyday conversation, {住民|じゅうみん} or {住人|じゅうにん} is more natural.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {海外|かいがい}{居住者|きょじゅうしゃ} (overseas resident)
- {居住者|きょじゅうしゃ}{専用|せんよう} (for residents only)
- {居住者|きょじゅうしゃ}{以外|いがい} (non-residents)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {住民|じゅうみん}: resident — general term for people living in an area, common in everyday use
- {住人|じゅうにん}: resident, dweller — slightly more casual, often for apartment or house residents
